A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same RoMaP research. Their complete main texts, supplementary sections S.1–S.4, algorithms, equations, tables and figures are readable and can be matched despite reflow and relocated references.

before.justification: v1 reports original editing and segmentation experiments, user studies, ablations and qualitative results in the main text and supplement.

after.justification: v3 retains these original empirical results, including Tables 1–3 and S.1–S.9 and the supplementary qualitative comparisons.

M1.justification: Both retain the same 3D-GALP segmentation, label-softness anchor sampling, Gaussian prior removal, masking and SLaMP-guided regularized SDS. Algorithms 1–2 and the associated procedures are unchanged.

E1.justification: Both use the same IN2N and NeRF-Art scenes, LERF and 3D-OVS complex scenes, CelebAMaskHQ images and generated-object editing scenarios. The appendix examples and task coverage are retained.

E2.justification: Tables 1–2 retain the same six editing and three generation baselines. Table S.7 retains LangSplat and LeGaussian; Table S.9 retains RePaint, IP2P, SD3-inpainting, Plug&Play and RF-inversion. No comparator membership changes.

E3.justification: Both retain 75 editing prompts, the same evaluation metrics and 260-respondent user studies. Appendix protocols also match: three-view segmentation evaluation and CelebAMaskHQ studies using 100 images for timing selection and 15 images for editing comparisons, each with 25 prompts.

E4.justification: The component ablation in Table 3, attention-processing ablation in Fig. S.4, SH-degree study in Table S.8, mixing-time sensitivity analyses and baseline failure examples are unchanged. Their relocation introduces no new analyses.

E5.justification: Both retain the same user-study Friedman and pairwise Wilcoxon tests in Fig. S.3 and statistical summaries in Fig. S.7. v3 adds no run counts, seed information, uncertainty estimates or statistical procedures.

E6.justification: Tables 1–3 and S.1–S.9 retain the same entries and values. For example, RoMaP's Table 1 scores remain 0.277 CLIP, 0.205 CLIPdir, 0.723 B-VQA and 0.674 TIFA. Qualitative results are also unchanged.

T1.justification: Equations 1–4 and the mathematical definitions of label softness, neighboring loss, regularized SDS and latent mixing are unchanged. Neither version contains additional theorems or proofs absent from the other.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same contributions and claims about precise, drastic part-level editing and improved controllability for reconstructed and generated Gaussians. The added code-access sentence does not alter scientific claims.

C2.justification: Mechanism explanations and interpretations are retained. Section S.4 states the same limitations involving 360-degree observations, complex geometry and blurry or poorly reconstructed scenes, alongside the same societal-impact discussion.

D1.justification: v3 adds a code-availability statement and project link at the end of the abstract, absent from v1. Implementation details, algorithms, hyperparameters and the single-A100 hardware disclosure otherwise remain unchanged. The PDFs establish the added access information, not the linked code's contents.

R1.justification: The same 68 references and related-work positioning are retained. Bibliography relocation and updated page backlinks do not change cited works or novelty positioning.

P1.justification: v3 moves References from before the supplementary material to the document's end and adds the abstract's code-access sentence. Scientific prose and the main and supplementary section hierarchy otherwise remain unchanged.

P2.justification: Supplementary body text is larger and reflowed, changing figure and table placements relative to prose. Printed page numbers disappear, and acknowledgements occupy a separate, mostly empty page. Figure content, captions and table structures are retained.

improvement.justification: The new RoMaP code-access pointer modestly improves implementation discoverability, and larger supplementary text aids readability. Scientific substance is unchanged. Reflow creates sparse pages and removes printed pagination, limiting the presentation gain; the supplied PDFs do not verify the linked code's completeness.
